description: Long-term rules improve stewardship while preserving public legitimacy.
Immediate advantage creates high inherited burden and weak future freedom.
Climate repair improves future freedom and ecological inheritance.
Technical systems become inherited constraints without reversibility.
Maintenance deferral raises future costs and weakens institutional capacity.
Repair and stewardship strengthen future freedom and legitimacy.
Youth participation expands future representation and democratic renewal.
Crisis governance erodes planning capacity and future-oriented accountability.
